name: Harald V
summary: Harald V reigned as a constitutional monarch and kept to the convention that he does not take party positions; his own speeches stress trust, community, democracy and the equal worth of all people. In his New Year's addresses and in his 2016 garden-party speech he welcomed diversity of origin, religion and sexual orientation, urged action on climate and the environment, and backed international cooperation and fairer sharing of goods. In 1997 he apologised on behalf of the state for the Norwegianisation of the Sami, and he spoke of reconciliation and Sami language rights later in his reign. Laws, throne speeches and other formal acts made on the government's advice are not counted as his positions.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In 2008 he said the easiest course is to ban what we dislike but that democracy is built on freedom to disagree ('prohibitions are the weapon of fear, tolerance that of security'); in 2014 he said Norway should keep a high ceiling for speech, even when it feels unreasonable, and that speech outside the criminal code should be answered rather than silenced. He also deplored hateful speech, so the evidence is not unambiguous.

empower-police-military.rationale: In his 2025 address opening the Sami Parliament he said Norway must invest more in the armed forces over the coming years; he did not address police or authority.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In 1997 he said the state must regret the injustice done to the Sami by its hard Norwegianisation policy and has a special duty to enable a strong Sami society; in 2023 he called for reconciliation work after the Truth Commission. This concerns an indigenous/ethnic minority rather than 'racial' injustice in general.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In 2016 he said that standing secure in awareness of one's own heritage makes it easier to meet others with an open mind; in 2018 he said the cultural treasure should be known, protected and passed on.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called the UN the most important common forum for peace and cooperation (2001), urged keeping its strong standing (1992), and in 1999 said the world has come far too short in binding cooperation and solidarity across borders.

limit-growth.rationale: In 2011 he said growth lifts millions out of poverty but that more and more suggests the Earth cannot bear further development like the one that created our prosperity; mixed with no call for limits as such.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2023 he said he shares young people's worry and impatience that adults are not taking strong enough measures, quickly enough, and hoped world leaders' targets would be followed by action; in 2022 he called climate the most serious issue and hoped for action in line with the seriousness.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Described the monarchy as having traditions and values to manage, rooted in the 1905 election of the king, and committed himself to the task for life (1991, 2022). This is his own account of his office, not an argument against alternatives.

democracy-best.rationale: In 2025 he quoted Churchill's line that democracy is the worst form of government except all the others, called it a system Norwegians want, and warned with alarm that democracy is being undermined worldwide. He did not address the case where voters choose badly.

ethnic-nation.rationale: In 2016 he defined Norwegians as including people who have immigrated from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria, among others, and said his own grandparents immigrated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: In 2008 he said we have a responsibility to protect nature for its own sake and that all nature and animal life has intrinsic value (egenverdi).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No recorded position. His general statements on equal worth do not address racial segregation laws.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: In 2012 he said different cultures should be able to live side by side and enrich each other, provided human rights are the guide; he did not call for giving up original culture.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: In 2008 he quoted the Universal Declaration on the right of adults to marry and found a family without restriction due to race, nationality or religion, and called free choice of spouse a human right.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In his 2019 New Year's address he said a free society must rest on all people being of equal worth, and held up the war as a warning of what an ideology of unequal worth leads to. In 2025 he added that all citizens should be equal before the law.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said in 2025 that Norwegians want a democratic system in which power proceeds from the people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: In 2001 he said the fight against poverty and for fairer distribution must be a prioritised task, including that children must not be excluded from school activities because of parents' finances.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In 2016 he described a Norway of great diversity as one people held together by trust, community and generosity; in 2019 he welcomed that Norwegians have become less alike; in 2012 he said different cultures can live side by side and enrich each other under human rights.

minority-language-support.rationale: In the speech opening the Sami Parliament (2017) he said the state has a duty to ensure Sami children get proper teaching in and of Sami, and called for enough Sami teachers and Sami-language competence in care services; in 2025 he named strengthening Sami languages as a priority for reconciliation. These are state-occasion speeches.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: In 2007 he urged widening the room for 'the normal' so more people can feel accepted for who they are; in 2012 he said individuals must not be allowed to limit others' way of living.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said in 2001 that the fight against poverty and for a more equal distribution of goods must be a priority both at home and globally; in 2006 that we should try to share goods more fairly and can solve world poverty if we work together; in 2005 that rich and fair distribution is a shared responsibility.

precautionary-principle.rationale: In 2005 he said nobody knows with certainty how serious climate change is, but that it is important to do our part anyway.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Described the palace as politically colour-blind when addressing MPs across parties (2013) and, at the start of his reign, made unity (samhold) the main aim of the king's work.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: In 1997 he said the Sami themselves should shape their own society and culture, and that the Sami Parliament should be able to decide within limits what values and skills Sami children learn in Sami schools.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Said in 2025 that the majority shall rule but minorities' rights must be protected, and that human rights give citizens rights and the authorities duties; he did not speak of courts directly.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: from his statements that the monarchy is a legitimate institution with succession within the family; he also noted that the modern monarchy originated in an election.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: In 2009 he said we have been better at counting our money than our days and that overconsumption may unbalance the climate; in 2001 he noted that increased wealth had not brought greater happiness.

religious-nation.rationale: In 2016 he said Norwegians believe in God, Allah, the Universe and nothing, and that all are Norway.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In 2015 he stated as fact that of 772 Norwegian Jews and Jewish refugees arrested and deported during the war only 34 survived, and warned about hatred of Jews today.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: from his 2016 statement that Norwegians include girls who love girls and boys who love boys, within a Norway that is 'us', and from his statement that all people are of equal worth.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Speaking in 2022 about his granddaughter's first Council of State meeting, he said he felt the strength and security in 'one generation following another', and told Ingrid Alexandra she represents the fifth generation of the monarchy.

racial-franchise.rationale: No recorded position. His general statements on equal worth do not address racial limits on voting.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: In 2008 he quoted the Universal Declaration on the right to marry without restriction due to race, nationality or religion, and called the free choice of spouse a human right.

future-generations.rationale: In 2009 he said we must hand the Earth on to new generations; in 2007 he spoke of defending the Earth's rights for grandchildren's sake.

women-suffrage.rationale: Marked the centenary of women's full suffrage in 2013 as a right fought for and an important constitutional change, and in 1999 praised the women pioneers who won the vote.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2001 he listed, among the aims Norway pursues through the UN, bringing war criminals to justice.

notes: Died 28 August 2026 (Wikipedia), so living is false and a few low-confidence inferences are marked 'Inferred:'. Only speeches he delivered himself (New Year's addresses, Storting-dinner speeches, the 2016 garden-party speech, commemorations) and the Sami Parliament opening speeches are used; the Sami Parliament speeches are state-occasion speeches and are therefore at most medium confidence. Throne speeches (trontale) and State-of-the-Realm statements were deliberately excluded as government-written. The 1997 Sami Parliament speech is the apology; it also contains passages that report government policy ('The Government has...'), which were not used. Kongehuset.no could not be fetched directly, so texts come from the Virksomme ord archive, which cites kongehuset.no as source. The 2003 and 2025 New Year's addresses were not retrieved. Wikipedia's note that he wished the constitution to keep requiring a Lutheran monarch is secondhand and was not used for any answer.
